speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, could you please describe your current symptoms, specifically focusing on the nature of your gait and limb ataxia? Additionally, please share any relevant details from your significant medical history that you believe might be related.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that you are experiencing right-sided clumsiness and a drunken gait. Have you noticed any other symptoms such as difficulty speaking, swallowing, or changes in your vision? Also, do you have a history of hypertension, diabetes, or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Crohn disease and long-term natalizumab use, I am concerned about the possibility of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). When did these neurological symptoms specifically begin, and have you experienced any changes in your memory, personality, or cognitive function?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with your history of natalizumab use, are diagnostic for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
